findings.title: Tray "Settings" can try to open a second settings dialog when one is already open.
findings.body: Hiding the window now keeps its state, so a settings dialog stays open while the window is hidden. That is the scenario in #467. If the user hides the window while settings are open and then clicks tray "Settings", this runs `ShowSettingsCommand.Execute(null)` again. `AsyncRelayCommand.Execute` does not check `CanExecute`, so a second dialog is pushed onto a `DialogHost` that is already open. That usually throws ("DialogHost is already open") or stacks dialogs. The exception is rethrown on the UI thread through the command's await-and-throw path and can crash the app. Before this change the window was recreated each time, so no dialog could be open at that point. Fix: only run the command when it can run, e.g. `if (_mainViewModel.ShowSettingsCommand.CanExecute(null)) ...`, or when no dialog is open.

findings.title: The `--start-hidden` hide check runs on every `Loaded`, not only at startup.
findings.body: `Window_OnLoaded` checks `StartOptions.Current.IsInitiallyHidden`, and that option stays true for the whole process. If Avalonia raises `Loaded` again when a hidden window is shown (in some Avalonia versions a `Window` gets `Unloaded`/`Loaded` on `Hide`/`Show`), then with `--start-hidden` every tray click or hotkey `Toggle()` hides the window again right away, and the user can never open it. Even if `Loaded` fires only once, the lifetime shows the window first and this handler hides it afterwards, so it can flash on screen at startup. I couldn't confirm from here which Avalonia version this uses and how it raises `Loaded`. Fix: use a one-shot flag such as `_isFirstLoad` so the hide happens only on the first load, or skip showing the window at startup when starting hidden.
